description: A corrected signed valuation closes the genuinely nonbinary primitive branch, and exact exceptional-chart sweeps close binary fixed factors of degrees one, two, and three, conditional on the upstream four-loci routing.

independent_review.scope: No independent review is represented in this public record.

manuscript_coverage.coverage_rule: Complete coverage requires an exact LaTeX location for every program-relevant defining claim. A locator records where the current statement and evidence boundary appear; it is not a proof-review status.

members.statement: In the primitive fixed-component branch P=GA, Q=GB with gcd(A,B)=1 and R=(H3)_3, write t=A/B and R^4/Q^3=rho(t). If an irreducible component Gamma occurs in G with multiplicity s and in the reduced special fiber A-xi B with multiplicity m, define c_xi=ord_xi(rho) for finite xi and c_infinity=ord_infinity(rho)+3. Then 4 nu_Gamma(R)=3s+c_xi m and the coefficients satisfy sum c_xi=3.
members.title: Corrected Valuation Identity for Primitive Quartic Fixed Components

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 four-loci reduction and the standard polynomial-centralizer theorem used in the proof note. Every genuinely nonbinary primitive fixed-component branch is closed: a fixed factor of degree two is eliminated by the corrected valuation identity or enters the existing same-fiber rank-one chart, while a fixed factor of degree one is aligned-automorphic, binary, or incompatible with the Keller condition.
members.title: Genuinely Nonbinary Primitive Fixed Components Are Closed

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 reductions reach a binary leading pencil whose greatest common divisor has degree three. After normalization H4=(xG,yG,0) with G in k[x,y]_3, every multiplicity type of G and every cubic R=(H3)_3 yields a polynomial automorphism or a triangular degree drop; hence this stratum contains no counterexample.
members.title: Binary Cubic Fixed Factors Are Automorphic

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 reductions reach a binary leading pencil whose greatest common divisor is a line. After normalization H4=(x^4,xB,0), with B a binary cubic not divisible by x, every quartic Keller map in the stratum is a polynomial automorphism.
members.title: Binary Linear Fixed Factors Are Automorphic

members.statement: Assume the Program 2 reductions reach a binary leading pencil H4=(P,Q,0) whose greatest common divisor G has degree two and whose residual binary quadrics are coprime. Then the residual pencil is a secant of the Veronese conic and may be normalized to P=x^2G, Q=y^2G; the generic first-normal complement and all four exceptional divisors QF1 through QF4 contain no counterexample, so the full Keller map is a polynomial automorphism.
members.title: Binary Quadratic Fixed Factors Are Automorphic
